cells.tense: You are holding the growing thing and the form it needs at the same time, right now.
cells.ask: Sketch what the next growing thing needs, with nothing old in the frame. Five minutes, paper or dry-erase, whatever's closest.
cells.core:
Something you were carrying the shape of is letting go — not torn out from under you, released. The room feels lighter than it should, and you're part of why. You're careful with what you water, patient with what's slow, and you don't confuse holding on with caring.

What came down left a gap, and the gap is already being worked in your hands. This is the thing working: growth without forcing, care that doesn't exhaust, space held without clutching. The credit for what you carried hasn't been spoken yet, and that's fine. It only needs to land somewhere, not be performed anywhere.

Sketch what the next growing thing needs, and let the credit for the hand that carried this one arrive when someone offers it. Nothing here is owed back.

cells.tense: Ahead of the clearing you've already rebuilt the thing, and you're bracing under its weight now.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you've been tending and let it stay unfinished for two days. Notice what the waiting actually asks of you — nothing more.
cells.core:
The collapse hasn't fully landed and you're already several rooms ahead of it, holding up the next version before anyone asked. You tell yourself this is care, staying ready for them. Some of it is. Some of it is gripping the pot instead of watching the plant.

Running well, this is care that doesn't exhaust — space held without clutching. The work you're doing is real; it's the pace that's ahead of the soil. Things can wait, and the waiting won't undo anything. Pick one thing you've been tending and let it stay unfinished for a couple of days, and find out what your hands do when they aren't holding it up.

cells.tense: You left the care behind you and still stand at the doorway, hands at your sides.
cells.ask: Put one small act of care on the calendar for tomorrow. Set it at whatever size fits the day, and let that size be enough.
cells.core:
The clearing came and you walked out of the room ahead of it. Since then your hands have stayed empty, and some small work that used to be yours quietly stopped. Nothing announces it — the plant just goes unwatered and you don't notice you've stopped noticing.

The care itself hasn't gone anywhere. Restarting it is smaller than it feels like, and it can start at whatever size fits the day. Working well, this is growth without force — patient, unrushed, not exhausting. The report can wait. Put one small act of care on the calendar for tomorrow and notice how much easier the next one is once your hands have moved.

cells.tense: You are already tending what's growing, and you have been describing it as simply how things are.
cells.ask: Answer, in front of someone who cares, what would have happened if you had stopped tending. Let the answer stand without deflecting it.
cells.core:
You've been calling it maintenance, just handling it, while you were the one deciding what got kept and what was let go. The structure came down and you were already at work in the gap — clearing it, keeping it from spreading — and your name didn't get put on that.

If you hadn't moved, the report would be different. One person who cares, one plain answer: what would have happened if you had stopped. Say it, let it land, and see if the room doesn't hold it. The credit for what you carried is already real; this is only the acknowledging.

A reader could reasonably say the dissolution isn't liberation for them at all, just loss, so each core leaves the object unnamed and lets them name it. The stray line was 'you already know who it was for,' which flatters the read and puts an answer in their mouth; it is gone.
